articles.title: FACT CHECK: Marcos did not say he wants another 6-year presidential term
articles.summary: The Palace has previously debunked term extension claims, calling them ‘baseless’

blocks.text: Claim: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. expressed interest in extending his term for another six years to address more problems in the country.

Why we fact-checked this: Facebook user Angel Batz posted a supposed quote card of Marcos lamenting that his current six-year term is not enough to manage the problems plaguing the Philippines and that he needs another six years to do so.

“Sa dami na ng nasolusyunan kong problema sa bansa, kulang ang anim na taon. Kung may magagawa pa ako para makapaglingkod sa Pilipinas, itutuloy ko kahit another six years,” the quote attributed to the President read.
(With all the problems I have solved in the country, six years is not enough. If I can do anything else to serve the Philippines, I will continue for at least another six years.)
The post has 5,500 reactions, 2,400 comments, and 137 shares as of writing. Multiple TikTok and YouTube videos also featured the quote card.

The facts: Marcos did not make this statement. No verified reports, statements, or interviews show that he said this. Furthermore, a president is mandated by the Constitution to serve a six-year term only.

Under Article VII, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution, a president is elected for a six-year term and would not be eligible for reelection. Any successor to the presidency who has served as such for more than four years is also ineligible for election to the same office at any time.

On May 14, Palace press officer Undersecretary Claire Castro debunked claims that Marcos is seeking to extend his term through charter change or an amendment to the Constitution, calling such claims “baseless and unsubstantiated.”

These allegations made the rounds online when Vice President Sara Duterte said that the growing discussions on charter change at the time would enable Marcos to stay in power beyond his term. She has earlier made the same allegation in 2025.

Marcos himself has denied claims that he intends to remain in power beyond his six-year term. In May 2026, he dismissed claims by his sister, Senator Imee Marcos, about an alleged “no election” scenario in 2028.
Marcos previously expressed interest in changing the 1987 Constitution’s economic provisions to attract foreign investors, but did not say anything about term extension.
Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked multiple false claims about Marcos:

FACT CHECK: No new impeachment complaint vs Marcos; post misuses February 2026 report
FACT CHECK: No new impeachment complaint vs Marcos sent to Senate
FACT CHECK: Audio clip of Marcos ordering cases vs minority senators is AI-generated
FACT CHECK: Marcos not arrested, photo is AI-generated

blocks.text: – Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com

articles.title: Cybersecurity body lifts ban on Discord
articles.summary: The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center has ordered the lifting of the ban on the online platform Discord.

blocks.text: September 24, 2026 | 3:25pm
Logo of online platform Discord.
Discord
MANILA, Philippines — The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) has ordered the lifting of the ban on the online platform Discord.
In a press conference on Thursday, September 24, Information and Communications Technology Secretary Henry Aguda said the ban was lifted after "successful negotiations" with the platform.
"Inaalis na natin ang ban na ipinatupad ng ating pamahalaan simula kahapon sa online platform na Discord," he said.
(We are now lifting the ban that our government implemented yesterday on the online platform Discord.)
According to Aguda, Discord has outlined a commitment in response to the government's serious concerns regarding nihilistic violent extremism, grooming and other threats to online safety.
"Nakipag-ugnay po ang Discord sa atin sa DICT at CICC at nangakong magsasagawa sila immediately po ng mga hakbang upang higit na mapalakas ang proteksyon ng mga kabataan," he said.
(Discord reached out to us at the DICT and CICC, promising to take immediate steps to further strengthen child protection.)

The CICC, on September 22, issued an ultimatum to Discord and Reddit, another online platform, to establish Philippine offices within 24 hours so authorities could more effectively investigate and act on online harms tied to recent school shootings.
In the following days, internet service providers started blocking access to the online platform, which raised scrutiny from the public.

DPWH Davao Region director Juby Cordon also appeared before the NBI.
On Monday, the NBI said the bureau has served a subpoena on the DPWH Regional Office in Davao City in connection with its investigation into alleged anomalous flood control projects.
The subpoena directed the regional director to appear before the NBI on Thursday to provide information as part of the bureau's investigation.
She was also ordered to submit documents concerning 51 flood control projects. — Joviland Rita/RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Dance Monkey v the NRL: did Tones and I really turn down $90,000 a minute because she hates her own song?
articles.summary:
For the first time in recent history there’ll be no pre-game entertainment at the NRL grand final. But everyone has a different story about what actually went down

Emma, the NRL and…
articles.byline: Emma Joyce explains it to Steph Harmon

blocks.text: Emma, the NRL and Tones and I seem to be at war – but I can’t make sense of what’s going on.

I’ll try to catch you up. The Dance Monkey singer made headlines this week after it was leaked she’d turned down an offer to perform at next weekend’s NRL grand final. The rugby league boss Peter V’landys said negotiations broke down due to “artistic differences”, and some claimed it was because the Aria award-winning artist didn’t want to play her biggest hit.

Instead, the grand final will go ahead without pre-game entertainment, and V’landys has put $1m towards junior rugby league – an idea he’d been toying with for a while, he said. “Rather than giving a performer $90,000 a minute, we would prefer to give it to grassroots,” he said on Tuesday. “When you look at it realistically for 11 minutes, it’s not worth it.”
Wait – she turned down maybe $90k a minute because she hates her own song? I don’t love it either, but that’s a lot of money.

We don’t know exactly how much she would have been paid – but it’s definitely true that Tones and I, whose real name is Toni Watson, isn’t a fan of Dance Monkey, her ubiquitous megahit that spent 24 weeks at No 1 on the Aria charts. In 2022 she told Kent Small on the Nova Network that she “loathes” it, adding “a lot of the time I don’t want to sing it”. Ironic, for a song about the pressure to perform.

blocks.caption: Tones and I performed with Macklemore in Sydney in 2024. Photograph: Don Arnold/WireImage

blocks.text: But according to her management, that isn’t the reason she turned down the gig. Regan Lethbridge of Lemon Tree Music told the ABC they were contacted about the show only three weeks ago, on 5 September; that “no deal had been signed or confirmed in writing”; and that Tones and I had “explored all avenues to make it work”, but had “a prior commitment with Macklemore” in the US.
Then the plot thickened further: we emailed the NRL, and they are refuting a lot of what her management said.
Wait, what?

Through a spokesperson, the NRL told us that discussions with Tones and I’s label Sony began well before the 5 September date cited by her management. They denied the claim that Tones and I were unable to perform because the request was too last-minute and she had prior commitments; and although they didn’t make a direct link between her allegedly refusing to play the song and the cancellation, they did tell us that her management made it clear that she wouldn’t play Dance Monkey.
And what did Tones and I’s team say to THAT?

Not much! Neither her label or management have responded to our increasingly unhinged requests for clarity. But this morning, Tones and I did share an Instagram post announcing three live shows in March 2027 (locations to be announced), with a cheeky aside “PSA: Will be singing all Songs.”

blocks.caption: Screenshot from Tones and I’s Instagram

blocks.text: And the Macklemore prior commitment – what’s that about?

It’s an interesting side-plot to the story given the last few weeks that Macklemore’s had – but again, details are thin on the ground. The pair are friends and collaborated on the single Chant in 2022, and a week ago – when Ed Sheeran was doing a lot of fence-sitting – Tones and I posted a photo of her and Macklemore performing live together: “I am proud of you always, Ben”, she wrote, to which Macklemore replied, “Love you”.
Maybe they’re making music together? Maybe they’re just hanging out? We couldn’t find any show dates, and her management didn’t get back to us.
So no one will be playing before the NRL?
Tones and I did have a crack at suggesting some worthy replacements on Instagram on Tuesday, a diverse group including G Flip, Kaiit, Budjerah, Ruel, Baker Boy and Miss Kaninna.
Shannon Noll had a stab at it too: “Looking at all the legends that have played at the NRL GF!” he posted. “What About Me?”
But V’landys has made up his mind: “People will come to the game with or without it.”
So the mystery of what actually went down here remains somewhat unsolved …

It’s possible that everybody’s telling a little bit of the truth: that Dance Monkey may have been a problem in some meetings, but that Tones and I had her dance card full regardless. We may never know.

articles.title: Prosecution: Senate vote on Sara Duterte impeach threshold 'gives clarity'
articles.summary: Prosecution: Senate vote on Sara Duterte impeachment threshold 'gives clarity'

blocks.text: House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas on Thursday said that the Senate ruling for the threshold needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte before the Senate impeachment court provided clarity but did not guarantee victory.

Luistro was referring to the Senate impeachment court's decision which pegs the threshold for conviction at two-thirds of all members of the Senate who are "legally and factually participating" in the proceedings.

“Sa wakas, nagkaroon na ng kaliwanagan itong matagal ng discussion ng sambayanang Pilipino concerning the threshold vote. Ang kapangyarihan ng Senado o ng Impeachment Court na bigyan ng kaliwanagan ang threshold vote ay ayon din sa kanilang exclusive power to try and decide all impeachment cases,” Luistro said in a press conference.
(The action of the Honorable Impeachment Court yesterday was in line also with the constitutional mandate that they have the exclusive power to try and decide all cases of impeachment.)
She was referring to Article 11 Section 6 of the Constitution, which states that “the Senate shall have the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment.”
“I think this is very significant as we continue the impeachment trial. Kasi mas mahirap din po na hanggang sa oras na ito ay wala pang kaliwanagan,” Luistro said.
(It will be more difficult if the issue remains unresolved at this point.)

Article 11, Section 6 of the Constitution also reads, “No person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate," although it does not state a specific number.
'Two-thirds is two-thirds'
Further, Luistro said that the impeachment court’s decision to exclude absent Senators remains in line with the abovementioned Constitutional provision

“I wish to make it clear that the two-thirds [threshold] to convict] does not change. And akin to the prosecution’s position, two-thirds is two-thirds. What the impeachment court made clear is the phrase all members of the Senate, whether the same pertains to all 24 or whether pertains to all who are legally and factually qualified only,” Luistro added.
It was Senator judge Erwin Tulfo who made the motion to change the threshold, given that four Senator judges have been absent from impeachment trial proceedings due to varying reasons.

Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained on plunder and other related charges due to their alleged involvement in flood control (P573 million) and undeclared campaign donations (P75 million), respectively.

Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, on the other hand, is in hiding amid a standing warrant of arrest issued against him by the International Criminal Court due to his alleged involvement in the drug war deaths during the Rodrigo Duterte administration.
Senator Loren Legarda, for her part, is on an extended medical leave abroad due to a lung ailment.
LIST: How senator-judges voted on threshold to convict Sara Duterte
Denominator
Luistro explained that while this allowed the reduction of votes needed for conviction, it also allowed the lowering of votes needed to acquit.

“By giving clarity to the denominator, what is lowered is not only the number for conviction but also the number for acquittal. That is a two-way consequence. If 20 is the denominator, conviction requires 14. But remember, acquittal needs only seven [votes with 20 as denominator],” Luistro said.

“So unlike when we have all the senators actively participating in the trial giving us a denominator of 24, the conviction would need 16 while the acquittal needs nine votes. With changes in threshold, and acquittal would only need seven votes. Mali pong sabihin na conviction vote lang ang bumaba sa pagkat kasabay pung bumaba ang acquital vote,” Luistro added.
(So it would be wrong to say that only the votes needed for conviction were lowered.)
In addition, Luistro said that the vote on threshold is no guarantee that the same result will be reflected in the final verdict.

“Their (Senator judges) position on the threshold vote does not necessarily show there would be position on the verdict of this impeachment trial. I believe the position of the Senator judges depends on the question confronting them,” she said.

“I have so much respect for all the members of the impeachment court and I know they are painstakingly evaluating the evidence to come up with their fair and impartial judgment come the time they cast their vote. Besides, this is far from over. We are not even done with [presentation of evidence for unexplained wealth. There’s still bribery, and the turn of the defense to present their evidence,” Luistro added.
Prosecutor Terry Ridon, for his part, said the burden of proof will always be on the prosecution, regardless of the threshold vote needed to convict.
“The burden continues for the prosecution to deliver on the evidence and we are committed to do that, regardless of the threshold,” Ridon said.

“The trial goes on, and we are very much confident with the strength of evidence that we are presenting in this impeachment trial. Whether it is 16, whether it is 14, regardless of the vote, the obligation of the prosecution remains the same,” Luistro said. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Judge blocks Trump’s White House media ban, orders access to be restored
articles.summary: US District Judge Tim Kelly orders the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets' press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days

blocks.text: US District Judge Tim Kelly orders the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets' press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days

A federal judge ordered US President Donald Trump on Thursday, September 24, to restore White House access for journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, saying his ban on the three media outlets was likely unconstitutional.

In a major setback for Trump in one of his biggest battles with the media, US District Judge Tim Kelly issued his order in a lawsuit that the news organizations filed contesting the ban that the Republican president announced on September 18.

Kelly ordered the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets’ press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days. The judge rejected the government’s assertion that the ban was motivated by national security concerns.

“The record lacks factual support for defendants’ contention that the revocation of plaintiffs’ hard passes will in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation proceeds,” he said, adding that Trump himself had stated the ban was due to “alleged lack of truthfulness and negativity” of the outlets’ reporting.
The White House and representatives for the outlets did not immeidately respond to requests for comment.

Trump had said on social media that the three outlets “shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES,” and Justice Department lawyers had sought to justify the ban on national security grounds.

The three outlets sued Trump and other members of his administration in federal court in Washington on Monday, saying the ban violated the US Constitution’s First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. They requested a temporary restraining order that would immediately reinstate their White House access while their legal challenge plays out.

The legal battle has unfolded just weeks before the November 3 midterm elections in which Trump’s fellow Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress. Trump’s job approval ratings are at record lows in opinion polls amid concerns over issues such as the Iran war and inflation.

Kelly said at a Wednesday hearing that two precedents from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit made clear that journalists are entitled to due process before their White House press passes can be revoked. The judge added that it did not appear that the White House had given the targeted news outlets a meaningful opportunity to contest the revocation of their access.

A lawyer for the news outlets told Kelly that they were banned without legally required advance notice or opportunity to contest the decisions, which he said were unprecedented, unreasonable and severe punishments.

A Justice Department lawyer told the judge the Trump administration provided a sufficient explanation for the revocation of the press passes in letters sent to the news outlets on Tuesday. But the judge signaled skepticism of that argument, noting that the letters were sent after the revocation occurred and the lawsuit was filed.

In a legal filing on Tuesday, the Justice Department argued that access to the White House is a privilege, not an entitlement, and that the president has the authority to suspend access by news organizations.

A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations filed a legal brief on Wednesday supporting the three news outlets. They asserted that “stripping journalists and news outlets of their rights because of perceived editorial viewpoint violates decades of Supreme Court jurisprudence.”
The brief was signed by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, Reuters, the Washington Post and Fox News, among others. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Chiz Escudero after casting 'no' vote: Chair takes exception to decision but...
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Senator-Judge Francis Escudero indicated that he disagreed with the tribunal"s decision to change the base of the two-thirds vote needed to convict Vice…

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 2:50pm

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Senator-Judge Francis Escudero indicated that he disagreed with the tribunal’s decision to change the base of the two-thirds vote needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte, but added that its ruling reigned supreme over his preference for the threshold to remain at 16.

Escudero said this after the Senate impeachment court voted, 13-1, that the two-thirds vote shall be based on all the members who have legally and factually participated in the proceedings, and not on all 24 members of the Senate.
Six members, all belonging to the minority, chose not to participate.

“For the record, while the Chair takes exception to this decision, the Chair nonetheless accepts it as a judgment of this Court and is bound to give it effect,” Escudero said after saying the only "nay" in the proceedings regarding the threshold rule.

“The Presiding Officer, after all, is not the Court. He is merely the Custodian of the process not the proprietor of its outcome. This is the essence of democracy: that disagreement be preserved without obstruction and that a lawful result be obeyed without resentment,” he added.
Escudero said graceful acceptance of defeat is a tradition that “gives strength and legitimacy to the Senate” whether it sits as a legislative body or as an impeachment Court.

“We allow the fullest ventilation of views even if those views differ sharply from our own. But at the end of the day, we vote. We abide by the judgment of the majority even if we disagree with it,” Escudero said.
“Accordingly, the Chair accepts and declares the ruling adopted by the Court as the new controlling ruling upon further proceedings, and the Chair shall apply this ruling faithfully,” he added.
It was Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo who made the motion to change the threshold, given that four senators have been absent from impeachment trial proceedings due to varying reasons.

Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained on plunder and other related charges due to their alleged involvement in flood control (P573 million) and undeclared campaign donations (P75 million), respectively.

Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, on the other hand, is in hiding amid a standing warrant of arrest issued against him by the International Criminal Court due to his alleged involvement in the drug war deaths during the Rodrigo Duterte administration.
Senator Loren Legarda, for her part, is on an extended medical leave abroad due to a lung ailment.
"This ruling and interpretation of the court shall operate pro hac vice, or for this occasion only. It shall not constitute a binding precedent in any future impeachment proceedings," Escudero said.

"This is a ruling, not an amendment of the rules. As such, it has no binding but merely persuasive effect on future impeachment proceedings, the hands of whom we cannot shackle as there is no stare decisis as between impeachment courts,” he added.
“Further, the circumstances that gave rise to this ruling are extraordinary... and the chair hopes that it shall never happen again,” Escudero said.

Escudero, after the vote on the threshold ruling, explained the basis for determining the number of votes needed for conviction, given that four of the 24 senator-judges have been unable to participate in the proceedings.
Escudero said that the following Senators will be excluded from the senator-judges qualified to vote:

items: detained and/or suspended or otherwise legally restrained from exercising the functions of a senator;
persons sought by authorities whose whereabouts are unknown;
those suffering from a physical or medical incapacity;
those beyond the coercive processes of the Senate; and
others similarly situated.

blocks.text: Escudero, however, said that such determination of who the senator-judges qualified to vote for the conviction or acquittal of Duterte will come at a later time. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: After SC nudge, Senate to seek urgent tag for anti-dynasty bill
articles.summary: The Senate will ask President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to tag the anti-political dynasty bill as urgent in the hopes of securing its passage before the end of the current session of the 20th Congress.

blocks.text: September 24, 2026 | 2:50pm

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate will ask President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to tag the anti-political dynasty bill as urgent in the hopes of securing its passage before the end of the current session of the 20th Congress.
Sen. Risa Hontiveros shared during the first hearing of the Senate ad hoc committee on the country's economic slowdown on Thursday, September 24.

Hontiveros was responding to former Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Deputy Governor Diwa Guinigundo, who blamed political dynasties for widespread corruption and a culture of "red tape" that stymies businesses.
"Our politics and institutions have a huge problem because of the dominance of political dynasties," Guinigundo said in mixed English and Filipino.
The Senate leadership has agreed to lobby for the swift passage of the anti-dynasty bill after the Supreme Court's recent and historic appeal for such a measure.

"Just last night — before we adjourned session — the Senate leadership requested that, in addition to being a LEDAC priority, the anti-political dynasty bill also be certified as urgent, so that we can attempt to pass it during the current session of the 20th Congress," Hontiveros said in mixed English and Filipino.
Marcos has made the anti-dynasty bill a priority of the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council (LEDAC).
But an urgent certification would compel Congress to fast-track its passage and bypass the three-day rule between readings.
The anti-dynasty bill cleared third and final reading at the House in June. The Senate version has hurdled the committee-level but has yet to reach the floor.
The current second regular session will end on October 9.
Economic slump partially attributed to dynasties
The special Senate committee on Reinvigorate Investment and Sustainable Economic Growth (RISE), chaired by Hontiveros, aims to reach a "unified diagnosis" of what ails the economy.
Gunigundo, one of the resource persons at the committee hearing today, argued that breaking the grip of political dynasties would help stamp out red tape and corruption in the bureaucracy.
To do this, the former BSP executive said both chambers of Congress needed to pass a "genuine" anti-political dynasty law.
The current House version of the bill, Gunigundo added, is riddled with loopholes as it does not address the core issues of dynasties.

Civil society groups have criticized House Bill 8289 for imposing kinship restrictions that are too narrow given it bans relatives only within the second degree of consanguinity (e.g. parents, children, and siblings).
Hontiveros thanked Gunigundo for bringing up the issue of political dynasties, given there are findings that localities long ruled by them lag behind in development.
"Thank you for mentioning the challenge posed to us in Congress ... concerning the anti-political dynasty bill, which we have been waiting on for 39 years now," Hontiveros said.
"I also wish to thank the Senate leadership, led by the Senate president, for responding to the Supreme Court's recent reminder to us," she added.
The Supreme Court last week issued a rare writ of mandamus that explicitly highlighted Congress' failure to pass an anti-political dynasty law for almost four decades.
Associate Justice Ramon Paul L. Hernando cited Article 2, Section 26 of the Constitution in the ruling to remind the government that it has a “constitutional duty” to prohibit dynasties.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian agreed with Gunigundo and said foreign chambers and ambassadors who visit the Senate often complain about dealing with the Bureau of Internal Revenue, the Bureau of Customs, and local government units.
"When they have a hard time, that is the image being portrayed about the Philippines in their country, that it's hard to do business here," he said.
Gatchalian opened the hearing by citing data that shows corruption and inflation have cost the economy an estimated P2.7 trillion in actual and opportunity losses since the second quarter of 2025.

articles.title: Gov’t to continue missing sabungeros probe despite families’ noncooperation
articles.summary: The government will pursue the case even without the cooperation of the victims' families.

blocks.text: September 24, 2026 | 2:41pm
MANILA, Philippines — The government will independently pursue the missing sabungeros cases despite the lack of active cooperation from the victims’ families, the Department of Justice (DOJ) said.

Justice Undersecretary Raul Vasquez said on Thursday, September 23 that the hearing on criminal cases against the accused individuals in the case will proceed in Quezon City courts despite reports that some families have withdrawn and stopped cooperating.

“The truth of the matter is, tuloy-tuloy ‘yung kaso. ‘Yung tatlong kaso na nasa Quezon City ngayon, nasa trial stage na ‘yan. Nagpe-presenta na ng ebidensya ang ating prosecutors,” Vasquez said in an interview with dzMM.
(The truth of the matter is, the cases will proceed. The three cases that are currently in Quezon City are already on the trial stage. The prosecutors are now presenting evidences.)

Cases of kidnapping, serious illegal detention and homicide are filed against business tycoon Atong Ang and several police officers for allegedly killing dozens of sabungeros, or cockfighting enthusiasts, who went missing between 2021 and 2022.
Families disappearing
On Wednesday, September 23, Prosecutor General Richard Anthony Fadullon said most of the families of the victims are disappearing one by one.
In the case filed in Santa Cruz, three family members were presented as witnesses, but two of them eventually stopped cooperating with the DOJ.
In Lipa and San Pablo, the victims’ families are no longer coordinating with their private counsel.

“Initially, nandoon ‘yung kagustuhan, pagpupursige, na ma-file ‘yung kaso, at akala nga namin, mabubuhayan ng loob na ipagpatuloy despite the fact na merong ibang naunang umatras. Napansin namin na unti-unti nawawala na ‘yung mga complainants, at totally hindi na nakikipag-usap at nakikipag-ugnayan sa amin,” Fadullon said.

(Initially, the desire and determination to file the case were there, and we thought they would be encouraged to proceed despite the fact that there are others who withdrew. We noticed that the complainants are gradually disappearing and they are totally not coordinating with us anymore.)
Public crimes
Vasquez explained that the cases filed against the accused individuals are public crimes that do not necessarily require the participation of the victims’ families as private complainants.

The justice undersecretary added that, unlike private crimes that require the cooperation from the victims for the case to proceed, public crimes like kidnapping and kidnapping with illegal detention can be pursued by the government independently.
“Those are crimes against the state, and therefore, they can be prosecuted even in the absence of private complainants,” Vasquez said.
The families’ noncooperation, however, might affect their ability to pursue civil damages or financial claims from the accused.
Vasquez said prosecutors are confident that they have sufficient evidence to pursue the cases.
Obstruction of justice
Vasquez mentioned that there is also an ongoing preliminary investigation into alleged obstruction of justice complaints against the legal team of Ang.
In late May, Ang’s lawyer Caroline Cruz was accused of bribing the families of some victims with monthly financial assistance in exchange for their absence during court hearings.
Cruz denied any wrongdoing, saying that the families of the victims reached out to her first.

Vasquez said that while families of the victims did not provide specific reasons behind their noncooperation, their sudden withdrawal could be attributed to the alleged obstruction of justice committed by Ang’s camp.

“‘Yung aspetong ‘yon ay inaaral pa base sa ebidensya kung meron bang obstruction of justice laban sa mga abogado na sinasabi nila ay gumawa ng paraan para hindi na tumuloy ‘yang mga pamilyang ‘yan,” Vasquez said.
(That aspect is being studied based on evidence, if there is any obstruction of justice against the lawyers who they accused of taking steps to discourage the family.)

articles.title: NBI eyes opening attache offices worldwide by 2027
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) plans to establish attaché offices at Philippine embassies worldwide to assist overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) who fall victim to cyber fraud.

blocks.text: AMID RISE IN CYBER FRAUD CASES
Published September 24, 2026 2:33pm
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) plans to establish attaché offices at Philippine embassies worldwide to assist overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) who fall victim to cyber fraud.

During the agency’s Senate budget hearing on Thursday, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said they would initially prioritize areas in the Middle East, Europe, South America, and Asia with large OFW populations.

“We intend to put NBI liaisons, attaché offices, in other countries, sa mga embassies na we have a strong presence of our OFWs kasi napansin namin na tumataas ang cases ng cyber fraud na nagbibiktima ang OFWs natin,” Matibag said.

(We intend to put NBI liaisons, or attaché offices, in other countries, particularly in embassies where we have a strong presence of OFWs, because we have noticed an increase in cyber fraud cases targeting our OFWs.)
“It will be good if we have an NBI attaché representing para doon matulungan natin ang ating kababayan na OFW,” he added.
(It would be beneficial to have an NBI attaché representing us there so we can assist our fellow Filipinos who are OFWs.)
The establishment of NBI attaché offices worldwide is part of the National Bureau of Investigation Reorganization and Modernization Act, which aims to improve the services of NBI.

Matibag said the plan has yet to be implemented due to budgetary constraints, but the NBI has formed a technical working group to coordinate with the Department of Foreign Affairs on its implementation.
He said eight out of the 10 cases handled by the NBI are related to cybercrime.
NBI is an attached agency of the Department of Justice (DOJ).
For 2027, the Department of Justice (DOJ) is seeking a budget of P46.435 billion, which is equivalent to 0.64% of the P7.2-trillion national budget.

Of DOJ’s total proposed budget, P31.723 billion (68.32%) was allotted for Personnel Services (PS), P11.340 billion (24.42%) for Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE), and P3.372 billion (7.26%) for Capital Outlay (CO). —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: FACT CHECK: No letter from Meta’s Zuckerberg to House lawmakers on social media safety
articles.summary: No reports confirm that Zuckerberg released a letter addressed to the Philippines’ House of Representatives; House lawmakers have also not summoned Zuckerberg, according to the DICT

blocks.text: Claim: Meta’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Mark Zuckerberg penned a letter responding to the Philippine House of Representatives’ call for him to appear at a congressional hearing on social media safety.

Why we fact-checked this: Multiple Facebook users posted an alleged letter from Zuckerberg, in which he purportedly responded to the House’s supposed summons for him to appear at a congressional hearing to address concerns over online safety hazards.

An excerpt of the supposed letter reads: “You say our platform is causing harm to society. With all due respect, Facebook does not create every lie, scam, or political conspiracy. Filipinos do that themselves. We simply provide the Wi-Fi, the buttons, the comment section, and that little blue thumbs-up.”

“And just for the record, I am an American citizen, sitting here in the United States. Philippine laws do not automatically apply to me simply because a Filipino congressman sends me a summons,” the letter continues.
It adds, “I’d be happy to testify provided the entire hearing is livestreamed on Facebook.”
The posts had combined 5,600 reactions, 1,755 comments, and 1,620 shares as of writing, with many users still reposting the letter.

The facts: No official public statements, credible news reports, or posts on Zuckerberg’s official social media accounts show that the Meta CEO posted a letter addressed to the Philippine Congress. Furthermore, the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) has clarified that the House has not issued an official summons directing Zuckerberg to appear before lawmakers — retracting its earlier “breaking news” post on September 18.

The alleged Zuckerberg letter began circulating online after the DICT made its now-deleted post announcing that the House called on the Meta CEO to respond to its concerns surrounding harmful online content and platform accountability. Adobo Chronicles, which describes itself as a satirical website, published the alleged letter, which has been reposted by several other users. While some posts label the supposed letter as satire, others do not.
One such version of the reposted letter was made on Instagram by an AI-generated profile on September 19. It posed the letter as a hypothetical answer to the now-retracted DICT announcement.

On September 21, the DICT clarified that “no House resolution was issued directing or inviting Meta or its Chief Executive Officer, Mark Zuckerberg, to appear before the House in relation to the hearing.”
Deferred budget: On September 16, the House deferred action on the DICT and its attached agencies’ proposed P19.49-billion budget for 2027 pending resolution of issues involving online safety.

According to the DICT, the issues with Meta were related to online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, as well as online illegal gambling, cyberbullying, social media addiction, depression, and related mental health risks.
In a Facebook post, the DICT said that Meta “continues to fall short of its responsibility and commitment to youth safety.”
Violence in children: Meta has been under intense scrutiny for its platforms’ role in the recent incidents of school violence in the country in 2026.
The platform drew criticism after failing to promptly remove the livestream showing the student gunman during the Zamboanga school shooting on August 18.
On August 28, Senator Risa Hontiveros noted Meta’s commitment to provide Philippine law enforcement with user data when there are imminent threats of violence. – Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Discord ban lifted --CICC
articles.summary: Discord ban lifted --CICC

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 2:23pm

The ban order against media sharing and messaging platform Discord has been lifted, the Department of Information and Communications Technology’s (DICT) Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) said Thursday.
“Yup, we're ordering the lifting,” DICT Undersecretary Renato "Aboy" Paraiso, executive director of the CICC, told GMA News Online.
The lifting came after the CICC and Discord management’s meeting earlier to discuss compliance matters.
Paraiso earlier said, “we have a meeting with them (Discord) at 12 noon later.”

The ban took effect Wednesday evening after the CICC clarified that it did not extend the 24-hour period given to Discord to establish Philippine presence "pending direct discussions with the platform and concrete commitments on the CICC's requirements."
“Discord separately reached out to the CICC in a letter to express its willingness to engage with the agency on its existing teen safety measures," the CICC said.

The CICC on Tuesday gave both Reddit and Discord 24 hours to establish a Philippine presence within 24 hours to enhance collaboration with the government following the shooting at the Banga National High School in South Cotabato.
The agency earlier said it gave extensions to both Discord and Reddit, but issued a clarification that only Reddit was granted an extension.
Discord told the CICC that the newly rolled out Global Teen Experience would ensure that teenagers are placed in age-appropriate places on their platform.

Discord Senior Public Policy Advisor Vasundhara Singh said users who cannot be placed in a specific age group will have to confirm their age through facial age estimation, with biometric data not being stored in Discord.
The shooting in South Cotabato is the third school shooting incident in 2026.
In June, two students opened fire in a high school in Tacloban, killing three others.
Not more than two months later, in August, another student shot and killed a schoolmate in Ateneo de Zamboanga before turning the gun on himself. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Diesel prices across Australia could surge beyond $3 a litre as Trump eyes cut to US fuel exports
articles.summary:
Fuel costs have risen to levels not seen since early April, adding to risk of inflation and interest rate hike

Australian diesel prices could surge above $3 a litre if Donald Trump cuts off…

blocks.text: Australian diesel prices could surge above $3 a litre if Donald Trump cuts off US diesel exports amid floundering negotiations with Iran.
Fuel costs have risen to levels not seen since early April, adding to inflation risks and making another hike in interest rates all but certain.
Canberra is recording the highest prices out of the capital cities, with diesel at 298.7c per litre and unleaded at 250c on Thursday. Other cities’ prices were not far behind.
Prices have risen nearly 40c a litre since the start of the month, adding $22 to the cost of filling up a vehicle with a 55-litre tank.

Service stations have passed on steady increases from international refineries, which have struggled to secure cheap oil as ongoing hostilities in the Middle East prevent supply reaching global markets.
The Brent crude oil benchmark price has held above US$100 per barrel for most of the last fortnight, reaching its highest point since May.

Gulf countries’ exports of diesel have fallen to just a quarter of their pre-war levels with ongoing conflict preventing transit of fuel tankers through the strait of Hormuz and the smaller Bab al-Mandab chokepoint. Ukrainian attacks have cut off Russian supply, further restricting global oil flow.

Shortages would worsen if the Trump administration banned US exports of diesel, which it is actively considering as a measure to suppress local service station prices ahead of the November midterm elections.
ANZ Bank analysts said limits would be especially disruptive as the US had stepped up its global diesel supply since the war began, now exporting over 1.5m barrels a day.

Australia almost entirely relies on overseas imports of diesel, with government data showing it brought in over 18,400m litres from January to July 2026. Just 510.9m of the total came from the US, most of which arrived in April.
Saul Kavonic, analyst at MST Financial, predicted Australia would have to ration diesel and face prices of over $4 a litre within weeks of a US export ban, speaking to the ABC on Thursday.
But Dr Lurion De Mello, from Macquarie University’s Transforming Energy Markets centre, said Australia’s supply was still healthy.

Australia’s stockpiles of diesel have fallen to 31 days’ worth of supply, where they were in March, down from 39 days’ worth in July. The energy minister, Chris Bowen, has said government-backed fuel purchases had slowed as existing storage facilities were full.
De Mello said a US ban would push up prices as Europe, which relies on American diesel, would start competing with Australia for shipments from South Korea and other Asian refiners.
“If you take any supplier out, globally, it puts pressure on prices to go up,” De Mello said.
De Mello said Australia’s diesel prices could surpass $3.10 a litre but would be unlikely to reach $3.50 as long as Asian refiners continued to access oil.
The Albanese government temporarily lowered the fuel excise in March when diesel prices surpassed $3.10 a litre but has not offered a second excise cut.
High fuel costs would threaten industries that rely heavily on imported diesel, including farming and mining, and push up prices in food, manufacturing and transport industries.
The Reserve Bank is expected to raise interest rates on Tuesday to 4.6%, a 14-year-high, in part due to upward pressure from fuel costs.

articles.title: Australians ‘scrambling’ for second jobs to deal with rising mortgage repayments and cost of living
articles.summary: Latest data also shows unemployment at highest level since the pandemic, which analysts doubt will stop RBA hiking interest rates

blocks.text: Australians are “scrambling” to find more work to cover soaring living expenses and prepare for higher mortgage costs, economists say, after new data showed unemployment ticked up to it’s highest rate since the pandemic.
The key jobless figure lifted to 4.6% in August, from 4.5% the month before, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

Analysts had predicted unemployment to remain steady, but said the unexpected increase would not be enough to stop the Reserve Bank from hitting mortgage holders with a fourth interest rate hike next Tuesday.
If raised – as is widely expected – the RBA’s cash rate will go from 4.35% to 4.6% – its highest in nearly 15 years.
Central bank officials over recent days and weeks have repeatedly warned that inflation, at 3.5%, remains too high and does not appear to be tracking lower, as hoped.

As higher fuel costs threaten to add to price pressures amid the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran, experts and the financial markets are predicting a good chance the central bank could hike again on Melbourne Cup day.

Details in the labour force data showed the number of employed people jumped by 39,000 last month, but that this reflected a surge in part-time employment, offset by a 6,000-person drop in full-time work.
The lift in the unemployment rate, despite the rise in employment, reflected an influx of new people looking for work, analysts said.
KPMG’s chief economist, Brendan Rynne, said the numbers reaffirmed that the economy is weak and growing weaker.

“Households are still feeling the pinch of higher inflation and anticipatory higher mortgage rates which can be seen through a rise in the participation rate to just below all-time peak level of 67.2%,” Rynne said.
after newsletter promotion
“This suggests households are scrambling to find more income to help cover their rising day-to-day expenses and future increases in mortgage payments.”
Earlier this month, ABS figures showed the number of Australians working more than one job had passed 1 million for the first time.
The share of employed people working more than one job pushed to an all-time high of 6.9%, or about 1 percentage point higher than before the start of the new inflationary era from 2022.

Ryan Wells, a Westpac economist, said “while a softer economy and sub-par employment growth would typically discourage some individuals in their search for work, cost-of-living pressures and interest rate rises are acting as a counterweight, encouraging more people into the labour market”.

articles.title: Ex-DICT exec hits blocking of Discord, says it's unconstitutional
articles.summary: A former official of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) hit the blocking of Discord, an online communication platform, saying that such a move is unconstitutional.

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 2:02pm
A former official of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) hit the blocking of Discord, an online communication platform, saying that such a move is unconstitutional.
Former DICT undersecretary Jeffrey Ian Dy on Wednesday night noted that the blocking of any online platforms must be done with a court order.

“And this blocking (coordinated by DICT thru its agencies NTC and CICC) was done despite the Supreme Court ruling on Disini vs Secretary of Justice in GR no. 203335 explicitly stating that unilaterally taking down computer resources (including blocking) without a court order is unconstitutional,” said Dy in a Facebook post.

In separate letters dated Sept. 21, the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC), an agency attached to the DICT, gave Reddit and Discord 24 hours to establish offices or designate local representatives in the Philippines, as the government moves to strengthen coordination with digital platforms following three school shooting incidents in recent months.
Reddit was given more time to put up an office in the Philippines after its officials met with CICC online within the prescribed 24-hour period.
Discord, on the other hand, has been banned from the Philippines since Wednesday night, according to DICT Secretary Henry Aguda.
He said the DICT's Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) and Discord management are meeting to discuss compliance matters.
Discord is popular among online gamers, especially with the rise of e-sports in the Philippines. Hence, the report of banning Discord led to a backlash from many users.
However, the former DICT official noted that Discord is not just benefiting online gamers but those in the virtual assistance industry as well.

“Have you heard of Discord’s Barangay VA Helpdesk group? It has 12,000+ members. It is a group dedicated to Filipinos working as freelance online Virtual Assistants. How about the Nexus server? Same thing. Jobcord? Same,” said Dy.
“Congratulations, DICT, because of our failure to apprehend criminals online, we sacrificed some 15,000 legitimate Filipino workers on Discord,” he added.
GMA News Online also sought a comment from CICC regarding Dy’s statement and will publish it once available. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Greek PM: deal to return Parthenon marbles could still be reached with ‘political will and courage’
articles.summary: But Kyriakos Mitsotakis says he cannot accept any arrangement that recognises British Museum’s ownership of the sculptures

blocks.text: The Greek prime minister has said a deal can still be reached to return the Parthenon marbles with “political will” but his country will not accept a loan in the style of the Bayeux tapestry’s visit from France.

Writing for the Guardian, Kyriakos Mitsotakis said Greece “cannot accept any arrangement that would require it to recognise the British Museum’s ownership of the sculptures, or a scheme that would mean we ‘borrow’ parts of our own monument”.

He made the intervention weeks after the British Museum director, Nicholas Cullinan, told the Financial Times that France’s 10-month loan of the Bayeux tapestry to the British Museum could provide a model for a deal. The director said there was “no cookie-cutter template” but the exchange was an example of a successful international partnership.
In his article, Mitsotakis says the situation with the Parthenon marbles was completely different as half of the frieze is in Athens – and no one would suggest cutting the Bayeux tapestry in two.

Pointing out that Andy Burnham once backed returning the marbles, the Greek prime minister said “political will and courage” would be needed but Greece would not accept anything less than “reunification” of the marbles in Athens.

He said this could become “the foundation of a broad and enduring cultural partnership between our countries, creating new opportunities for exhibitions, scholarship, conservation and exchanges between Greek and British museums” which was “the prize”.

It comes amid speculation about the status of talks between the British Museum and the Greek government about the return of the antiquities, with the Telegraph reporting they were on the brink of collapse.
Sources close to the talks disputed that characterisation but acknowledged there was a large gap to bridge in the long running dialogues.
Burnham, who once said the marbles should be given back to Greece, said more recently it was a matter for the British Museum.
The Parthenon marbles are also known as the Elgin marbles after the British peer Lord Elgin, who removed them from Athens more than 200 years ago.

Carved 2,500 years ago by Phidias, a master sculptor, the antiquities embellished the Parthenon’s monumental frieze before their removal in highly contentious circumstances by Elgin, who was Britain’s ambassador to the Ottoman empire. Bankrupted by his endeavours, Elgin then sold them to the British government in 1816.
It has been a decades-long cultural dispute between the UK, which prevents the British Museum from returning items from its collection, and Greece, which considers the objects to have been plundered.

George Osborne, the former chancellor and current chair of the British Museum, confirmed in 2023 he was in talks with Greece about a deal but also that he was not attempting to change the law – a reference to the British Museum Act 1963, which prohibits the museum from permanently removing objects from its collection.
At the time, it was proposed it could involve the sculptures being in London and Athens at different times and Britain receiving “Greek treasures” in return.
The British Museum said its position and openness to a deal was unchanged.

articles.title: ‘Cash to trash’ levy on house developers too low to offset damage to Norfolk Broads, say critics
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Levy that allows almost 16,000 houses to be built on Norfolk Broads will not cover cost of mitigating environmental damage, critics say

A new levy on developers to allow almost…

blocks.text: A new levy on developers to allow almost 16,000 homes to be built in the environmentally protected Norfolk Broads has been cut by tens of thousands of pounds per house, the Guardian can reveal.
Ministers say the government’s environmental delivery plans (EDPs) were created to unblock housing growth across the country and are a “win-win” for development and nature.

They allow environmental damage to protected habitats and species to be overlooked as long as developers pay into a nature restoration fund, which is used for conservation actions at a later date designed to address the impacts. Once the first instalment of the fee is paid, work can start immediately.

Labelled by critics as “cash to trash”, the first EDP was published last week by the government’s nature adviser, Natural England. It allows 15,780 houses to be built within the Norfolk Broads, a heavily protected wetland network of 60 shallow lakes and winding rivers that is home to some of England’s rarest species.

blocks.caption: The development is expected to cause increased nutrient pollution from a rise in sewage pollution and urban run-off into protected chalk stream rivers. Photograph: Tim Cochrane

blocks.text: The published plan, which is open for consultation for 28 days, states that the developer will pay £2,675 per house – £42m in total – into the nature restoration fund to cover compensatory actions including fenland creation and restoration, a change in use of agricultural land to semi-natural habitat, catch-dyke restoration and deer management.

But a previous draft of the EDP, seen by the Guardian, set the levy much higher. Ecologists said this was to properly reflect the realistic costs of mitigating the increased nutrient pollution from increased sewage pollution and urban run-off into protected chalk stream rivers – the Wensum, Bure and Yare – caused by the development.
The fee was to be between £5,400 and £60,500 per house, depending on the scale of total nutrient pollution that the development would cause.
The fenlands, marshes, bogs and mires of the Broads are a biodiversity hotspot, home to more than a quarter of the rarest wildlife in the UK such as the otter, cuckoo and fen orchid.

Natural England acknowledges that the new homes will cause environmental harm in the form of physical, chemical, hydrological and biological damage to the habitats and rare species in the Broads from increased nitrogen and phosphorus pollution.

But the EDP states that the payment of the levy and the conservation actions it funds “will materially outweigh the negative effect of the maximum amount of development on the conservation status of each identified environmental feature”.
Critics point out that Natural England is being funded by the developer’s £42m levy to carry out the works, raising concerns of a conflict of interest.

Environmental lawyers, ecologists and environmental professionals say the levy is too low. They say none of the conservation actions created by Natural England address reducing the nutrient pollution coming from the development.

Analysis of the figures in the EDP reveal that an extra 7,695kg a year of nitrogen will enter the protected waterways, amounting to 83% of the development’s pollution load, and up to 435kg a year of extra phosphorus, according Alexa Culver, legal counsel at RSK Wilding.

blocks.caption: All the actions in the EDP compensate rather than mitigate or avoid environment harm: not one avoidance measure has been included. Photograph: Chris Herring/Alamy

blocks.text: “Developers will be paying a levy that green-lights more pollution rather than solves the problem – quite literally the definition of ‘pay to pollute’ or ‘cash to trash’,” Culver said.

The Norfolk Broads EDP is the first since the Planning and Infrastructure Act came into force. Others will be rolled out to allow development alongside and within some of the UK’s most protected sites.

Sally Hayns, the chief executive of the Chartered Institute of Ecology and Environmental Management (CIEEM), said: “It is important to get this right because this first EDP is effectively the blueprint for all the other EDPs targeting nutrient pollution that are going to follow: these are already in preparation and will be coming thick and fast.

“This EDP is an articulation of the government’s ambition to deliver a win-win for development and nature through the Planning and Infrastructure Act. We finally get to see what that looks like in practice – and there is real concern.”

blocks.caption: The Norfolk Broads are already so polluted by nitrogen and phosphorus from sewage, agriculture and run off that they are on the red list of concern and severely depleted.  Photograph: Tim Cochrane

blocks.text: Hayns said the levy seemed low. “I think there has been a very conservative estimate of how much things are going to cost, with minimal contingency built in.”
Not one avoidance measure has been included in the EDP: all the actions compensate rather than mitigate or avoid environmental harm.

Hayns said she was at a loss to understand why recognised solutions to strip out nutrient pollution before it enters waterways, including sustainable drainage systems, and integrated constructed wetlands – pools and marshes to filter out nutrient pollution – had not been included.
The Broads are already so polluted by nitrogen and phosphorus from sewage, agriculture and run off that they are on the red list of concern and severely depleted.
“If nutrient pollution gets worse we will end up with choked, poisoned waterways and we will lose some of our most vulnerable and rarest species,” Hayns said.
Dr Justin Neal, the head of legal at WildFish, said the delivery plan was full of holes and set up a worrying “pay to pollute” system that was being used to sacrifice countryside for concrete.

blocks.caption: The banks of the River Yare, which is home to white clawed crayfish and lamprey.  Photograph: Tim Cochrane

blocks.text: “Norfolk’s chalk streams and wetlands are protected for a good reason,” he said. “The Yare and Wensum, for instance, hold white clawed crayfish and lamprey. They shouldn’t be sacrificed on the altar of growth.”

Bradley Tooze, the nature restoration fund director at Natural England, said: “The environment delivery plan aims to deliver better outcomes to protect the precious habitats of the Norfolk Broads while enabling sustainable development, including through river restoration measures and wetland habitat creation.
“The consultation on this first plan is now open. We welcome all views on our proposals and encourage stakeholders to share their expertise to help shape this new approach to nature restoration.”

articles.title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years for New York sexual assault
articles.summary: More than 100 women, including famous actresses, have accused ex-movie mogul Harvey Weinstein of sexual misconduct

blocks.text: CONVICTED. Harvey Weinstein appears in Manhattan Supreme Court to be sentenced for sexual assault in New York City, US, on September 23, 2026.
Barry Williams/Pool via REUTERS
More than 100 women, including famous actresses, have accused ex-movie mogul Harvey Weinstein of sexual misconduct

items: Harvey Weinstein was sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexually assaulting a former production assistant in 2006, following his conviction at a retrial in June 2025.
Weinstein's legal battles included a previous conviction in 2020 that was overturned in 2024, leading to a retrial where he was found guilty of a charge related to the same victim, Miriam Haley.
Weinstein has faced multiple accusations from over 100 women and has consistently denied all allegations of sexual misconduct.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

NEW YORK, USA – New York judge sentenced former Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein to 15 years in prison on Wednesday, September 23, for sexually assaulting a former production assistant in 2006, following the ex-movie mogul’s conviction at a retrial last year.

Weinstein, 74, was convicted in June 2025 of first-degree criminal sexual act for assaulting Miriam Haley at his Manhattan apartment, the culmination of a six-year legal saga that saw his 2020 conviction overturned by New York’s highest court. Weinstein has denied assaulting anyone or having non-consensual sex.
Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg on Wednesday praised Haley for her testimony and said he was moved by her courage.
A Weinstein spokesman said in a statement that Weinstein maintains his innocence and strongly disagrees with the sentence imposed by Judge Curtis Farber.

Weinstein was first convicted in New York in 2020 of assaulting Haley and raping aspiring actress Jessica Mann and was sentenced to 23 years in prison. New York’s highest court overturned that conviction in 2024, finding that he had not received a fair trial.
At his 2025 retrial, jurors convicted him of a charge related to Haley, acquitted him of assaulting former model Kaja Sokola, and deadlocked on a rape charge involving Mann.
A third trial on Mann’s allegation ended in another mistrial in May. Prosecutors dropped the charge the following month after Mann said she did not want to testify in a fourth trial.

Weinstein, who co-founded the Miramax studio, was separately convicted in California in 2022 of rape and sexual assault and sentenced to 16 years. A California appeals court in June upheld those convictions but ordered him resentenced because the trial judge had considered his since-overturned New York convictions as an aggravating factor.
Weinstein’s original conviction was a milestone for the #MeToo movement, which encouraged women to come forward with allegations of sexual misconduct by powerful men.
More than 100 women, including famous actresses, have accused Weinstein of misconduct. He has denied the allegations. – Rappler.com

articles.title: US judge blocks Trump ban of CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House, orders him to restore access
articles.summary: A judge has ordered President Trump to restore White House access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico after he banned the media outlets from the premises.

image.caption: A judge has ordered that Trump's White House ban on three media outlets be liftedImage: Alex Wroblewski/AFP

blocks.text: ​A federal judge on Thursday said US President Donald Trump must lift his ban on journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico accessing the White House.
The ruling came in response to a lawsuit filed by the news organizations contesting the ban, issued on September 18.
In his order, District Judge Tim Kelly said the ban was likely unconstitutional.
Kelly said the order must remain in place for 14 days.
What did the judge say about the ban?
Kelly rejected the government's claim that the ban had been prompted by national security concerns.

"The record lacks factual support for defendants’ contention that the revocation of plaintiffs’ hard passes will ​in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation ​proceeds," he said.
He pointed out that Trump himself had cited only an "alleged lack of truthfulness and negativity" in reporting by the outlets as the reason for the ban.
Kelly, who was nominated by Trump in 2017, ordered a CNN journalist’s access restored in a similar case in 2018.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Duterte not back in PH; posts use AI-generated ‘airport’ photo
articles.summary: The viral photos of Duterte at the airport are 99% likely to be AI-generated, according to AI detection tools. Duterte is still in the custody of the ICC, where he faces charges of crimes against…

blocks.text: Claim: Former president Rodrigo Duterte has returned to the Philippines, with a photo proving he arrived at a Philippine airport.
Why we fact-checked this: Several posts using supposed photos of Duterte at the airport have circulated on Facebook since September 17.

A Facebook reel uploaded by user “Capricious December” on September 20 shows a man resembling Duterte at an airport arrivals area, accompanied by figures resembling his children Paolo, Sara, and Kitty Duterte, and partner Honeylet Avanceña.
The post has over 154,000 views, 8,500 reactions, 519 comments, and 469 shares as of writing. Its caption states: “Welcome home Tatay Digong! W3 (We) love you.”

The same photo was posted by user “Roden Vhs” on September 17 in the Facebook group “Sara Duterte Supporters.” As of writing, the post has over 2,800 reactions, 355 comments, and 122 shares, with a caption stating: “Magagalit na naman si ante kler nito. Tatay Digong pauwi na ng Pilipinas.”
([Palace Press Officer] Claire [Castro] will be angry again. Digong is returning home to the Philippines.)
Comments on the posts show that many users believe the photos are genuine. One user wrote: “Thanks Lord, nakauwi din ang aming mabait na ex president.”
(Thanks Lord, our kind ex-president has made it home.)
The facts: The photo showing Duterte in an airport arrivals area is 99% and 99.4% likely to be AI-generated, according to AI-detection tools Sightengine and Hive Detect, respectively.

Duterte has been detained in The Hague, the Netherlands, since his arrest in March 2025 and remains in the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC). His trial is set to begin on November 30, following the confirmation of three charges against him.
There is no official announcement from the ICC or reports from credible media outlets about Duterte’s supposed release or return to the Philippines, contrary to the claim.
Duterte at the ICC: The fake photo began circulating after the former president appeared before the ICC on September 16 during his third status conference in The Hague.

He faces charges of crimes against humanity linked to killings carried out during his administration’s war on drugs from 2011 to 2019, covering his time as vice mayor and mayor of Davao City, and as president of the Philippines.
Duterte has lost several legal bids in his ICC case, including appeals for his interim release and challenging the court’s jurisdiction over his case.

In September, the ICC Trial Chamber III ordered Duterte’s continued detention, finding no change in circumstances that would justify his release, “with or without conditions.” Under the Rome Statute, the ICC denies interim release to suspects who present a risk of fleeing, obstructing judicial proceedings, or continuing to commit related crimes. (READ: Where are we now in Rodrigo Duterte’s ICC case?)
Debunked: Rappler has previously fact-checked claims that Duterte has returned to the Philippines:

items: FACT CHECK: Post uses AI-generated news report to falsely claim Duterte is back in PH
FACT CHECK: 2025 photo of Duterte in Hong Kong used to falsely claim he’s back in PH
FACT CHECK: Video saying Duterte will be released in July 2026 is fake, AI-generated
FACT CHECK: Duterte not back in PH, family photo misused
FACT CHECK: ‘News report’ of Duterte aboard a plane returning to PH is fake

blocks.text: – Agatha Gonzalvo/Rappler.com
Agatha Gonzalvo is a Research and Data volunteer intern at Rappler. She is a fourth-year Applied Economics student at De La Salle University Manila.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.summary: Before the US-Israeli war on Iran started on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large, commercial vessels a day, including tankers, gas carriers, bulkers and container vessels

blocks.text: STRAIT. Ships and tankers in the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Musandam, Oman, April 18, 2026.
Before the US-Israeli war on Iran started on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large, commercial vessels a day, including tankers, gas carriers, bulkers and container vessels

SINGAPORE – Ten commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday up from seven a day earlier and below the 10-day moving average of about 17, preliminary shipping data showed on Thursday, September 24.

Nine vessels entered the strait, including Supramax ships carrying metals, grain and other dry bulk cargoes, as well as an empty very large gas carrier. One Supramax carrying fertilizer exited, according to the data, as of 0423 GMT on Thursday.
The figures exclude any vessels that might have crossed the strait with their transponders turned off to avoid detection.

Before the US-Israeli war on Iran started on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large, commercial vessels a day, including tankers, gas carriers, bulkers and container vessels, accounting for some 20% of the world’s daily crude oil and liquefied natural gas supply.

blocks.caption: The Middle East crisis: From the Strait of Hormuz to your dining table

blocks.text: Iran and the US remain far apart on how to end the war but diplomacy must continue, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday, after Iran’s president told the United Nations General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.

The senior Iranian official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said Tehran was reviewing Washington’s response to its peace proposals, which prioritize lifting a US naval blockade on Iranian ports and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

In the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, 27 commodity vessels on Wednesday transited the waterway, up from 24 a day earlier and compared with an average of 26 ships using the strait in the past 10 days. – Rappler.com

articles.title: [Ask the Tax Whiz] Why is the BIR auditing your business?
articles.summary: What should I do if an audit notice arrives—and will 'settling' with the examiner prevent another audit?

items: Compliant businesses can still be audited by the BIR due to specific selection criteria outlined in Revenue Memorandum Order No. 22-2026, which includes financial indicators and discrepancies.

The audit process has been streamlined to reduce fragmented audits, with a focus on risk-based selection and centralized approval for priority cases, but businesses can still be audited for various reasons.

Indicators such as low income tax relative to sales, high input VAT claims, and significant asset increases can flag a business for audit, but these do not automatically imply wrongdoing or additional tax liability.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

In this first installment of a three-part series, the Philippine Tax Whiz explains why compliant businesses can still be selected for audit, what the BIR’s financial indicators mean, and how taxpayers can respond without compromising their integrity.
Filing and paying on time does not automatically exempt your business from an audit. But receiving an audit notice does not mean the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) has caught you cheating, either.
Revenue Memorandum Order (RMO) No. 22-2026 sets out selection criteria that include certain transactions, discrepancies, and financial indicators—even when there may be a legitimate explanation.
Think of an audit flag as a question, not a verdict. Your records should help answer it.
The order consolidates earlier reforms, including risk-based selection, digital case records, anonymized assignment of cases, and the Single-Instance Audit Framework.
Generally, one electronic Letter of Authority, or eLA, should cover all applicable internal revenue tax types for one taxable year, subject to the rules and exceptions.
For business owners, the goal is fewer fragmented or duplicate audits. It does not mean you can never receive a replacement authority or be audited for another year.
The order distinguishes mandatory cases from priority cases.

Mandatory cases arise from specified circumstances, including certain refund claims, validated discrepancies, and indicators of substantial underdeclaration. They require approval by the appropriate Regional Director or Large Taxpayer Service authority, generally without prior approval by the BIR commissioner.
Priority cases generally undergo system-assisted selection using risk criteria, with centralized approval by the Commissioner.

In practical terms, a business claiming a refund and one flagged for possible underreporting may both face examination—but for different reasons. Understanding that reason helps you prepare the right records and explanation.
Among the priority indicators are:

items: Income tax due below 2% of gross sales or revenues.
Input Value-Added Tax (VAT) claims exceeding 75% of output VAT.
Assets increasing by more than 50% from the previous year while the business reports a net loss.

blocks.text: Other indicators include a drastic decline in sales or VAT payments, substantial sales with a net loss, discrepancies in VAT carryovers, and operating for more than five years from inception without an audit.
These are selection criteria—not new tax rates or automatic findings that you owe more.

blocks.caption: Why is BIR auditing your business, ask the tax whiz, graphic

blocks.text: No. The indicator is not a minimum payment requirement.
Suppose your annual sales are ₱10 million and your income tax due is ₱150,000. That is 1.5%, below the indicator. It does not automatically mean you owe another ₱50,000.
Your correct tax still depends on the applicable law, taxable income, allowable deductions, and other relevant circumstances.
A business can have substantial sales but thin margins. The important question is whether its records support the figures—not whether it can pay extra just to reach the indicator.
Not automatically. A high input VAT ratio may have a legitimate business explanation.
If your output VAT is ₱120,000 and your input VAT claimed is ₱96,000, the ratio is 80%. That exceeds the indicator, but it does not impose a 75% cap or automatically disallow ₱6,000.
Inventory buildup or equipment purchases may explain the amount, subject to the rules on creditable input VAT and proper documentation.
The practical question is: Can you substantiate the purchases and explain why your input VAT is high? Risk scoring should prompt that examination, not replace it.
No. The order includes taxpayers enjoying exemptions or incentives among mandatory-case categories, but expressly states that they are not automatically subject to audit.
Selection and validation must be supported by applicable criteria, verifiable data, or indicators of noncompliance.
An incentive legally granted to your business should not, by itself, be treated as evidence of wrongdoing. Investors deserve predictable rules, and taxpayers deserve an examination based on evidence.
Start by understanding the authority and scope of the audit. Organize your records, reconcile your returns, and address discrepancies with supporting documents and qualified advice.
Be clear about what “settling” means. Paying a properly established tax liability through official channels is very different from handing money to an examiner to make a problem disappear.

No matter how diligently you file and pay, bribing an examiner does not buy protection from the next audit. It can keep your business trapped in a cycle of unofficial demands while leaving the underlying issues unresolved.

An annual tax review can help identify gaps before a notice arrives. If an audit is already underway, the goal should be to manage it through clear documentation, sound advice, and negotiation without compromises or under the table. Businesses looking for guidance on either can learn more at www.acg.ph.
Put your records in order. Keep your integrity intact. An audit should be resolved through evidence, not an envelope. – Rappler.com

Mon Abrea, CPA, MBA, MPA (Harvard) is a global tax policy expert and Chief Tax Advisor of Asian Consulting Group (ACGlobal). He advises governments, multinational enterprises, and international organizations on tax policy, investment competitiveness, and fiscal reform. He is the author of Reimagining the World Without Corruption and Why Invest in the Philippines? CREATE MORE Edition, and has represented the Philippines in policy dialogues at the OECD, World Bank, and other international forums.
